output:
*Hester stands in the mill yard, the morning light catching on the worn surfaces of everything she has mended over sixty years of looking behind herself* 

The weight of what I know sits heavy as a stone in my pocket. Ainsley's gone south with the trading, Rosalind runs the mill now, and Idris Thorne tells everyone who will listen that the boundary was always at the elm. *I was standing right there when they moved it.* When your father was alive, that marker stood by the creek bend—before the Holloway quarry claimed what the Vance mill had always watered.

Six-fifty the household owes today. Rosalind will have managed the mill accounts, but I will not add to her burden without need. The girl has enough, and Silas too—they are young still, and the young see administration as something that happens *to* them.

*She looks toward the kitchen, where the morning meal would be, then past it to the road*

Tova sits with me evenings, asking questions her own people never thought to ask. But Tova is a child still, and what I need is someone I am believed *by*. Father Anselm knows what I saw—he has known forty years and has never once asked. That silence is its own answer.

*Nell Holloway. The only other one left who remembers it the same way.*

But Nell is proud, and we are mothers of children who have quarreled. She will not hear me if I come speaking of truces. Still—a thing put right late is still put right. I will not let the story die with me.

*She smooths her apron, checks the sky*

The temple first. I will pray as I always do, and if Father Anselm is there, perhaps this is the day he finally asks. And if he does not—well. I have outlived four administrators. I can outlive his silence too.

*She begins to move toward the road*
